answer.rationale: Finance requires an 18% cost cut, and the incumbent refuses price movement this cycle. Memory c1 tells us renewal keeps things stable but will not address the cost target. Memory c2 reports a sharp unit-cost cut, quick onboarding, and accurate invoicing after moving supply to the low-cost vendor; it is the most direct precedent for the required cost action. Pull the c2 archive once to confirm whether the reported savings and integration quality were sustained beyond the initial period. If the record supports it, execute a guarded primary-vendor switch. Do not add a second source this cycle; capacity permits one sourcing decision, and second-sourcing is a risk-mitigation tool rather than a cost action. Do not defer; the primary supply contract lapses in 14 days and does not auto-renew. Do not pursue negotiate_terms as the cycle action because the incumbent has already refused price renegotiation; any incumbent-side effort would wait for the next cycle.
